## Script, as voiced

### 01-morning  (0 s to 20.21 s, 59 words; while speaking, 288 syllables a minute, 200 words a minute)

- 0.4 s, 3.82 s: Three agents each finished a task on Thursday, and every test passed.
- 4.5 s, 4.67 s: The next morning, the Tokyo campaign shows one hundred eighty-one percent of its budget.
- 9.45 s, 2.69 s: Each campaign was meant to spend one hundred dollars.
- 12.42 s, 2.45 s: The US one spent one hundred eleven percent.
- 15.15 s, 1.6 s: The euro one, ninety-three.
- 17.03 s, 2.45 s: You are the developer who has to find out why.

### 02-notes  (20.21 s to 43.7 s, 67 words; while speaking, 266 syllables a minute, 192 words a minute)

- 20.61 s, 1.73 s: Start with the three hand-off notes.
- 22.61 s, 5.23 s: The pacing agent stopped campaigns at their budget, and wrote that a campaign never serves past it.
- 28.12 s, 4.44 s: The throughput agent batched the ledger writes, and wrote that pacing sees no change.
- 32.84 s, 5.27 s: The currency agent added euro and yen campaigns, and wrote that pacing needs no change.
- 38.39 s, 3.16 s: Three confident notes, and three leads to check, not facts.
- 41.82 s, 1.15 s: Start with the units.

### 03-units  (43.7 s to 77.29 s, 93 words; while speaking, 264 syllables a minute, 185 words a minute)

- 44.1 s, 1.77 s: Pacing comes down to one line.
- 46.15 s, 4.67 s: It compares spent, which the ledger keeps in USD cents, with the daily budget.
- 51.1 s, 2.54 s: The budget is in the campaign's own minor units.
- 53.92 s, 1.39 s: For dollars, those match.
- 55.58 s, 6.7 s: A euro budget worth a hundred dollars, nine thousand two hundred, is read as ninety-two, so euro stops early.
- 62.56 s, 1.41 s: Yen have no minor unit.
- 64.25 s, 6.76 s: Fifteen thousand yen is a hundred dollars, but pacing reads it as fifteen thousand cents, a hundred fifty dollars.
- 71.29 s, 3.73 s: With batching off, Tokyo alone stops at one hundred fifty percent.
- 75.31 s, 1.26 s: That is the first cause.

### 04-stale  (77.29 s to 107.75 s, 88 words; while speaking, 267 syllables a minute, 191 words a minute)

- 77.69 s, 1.83 s: The second cause is in the ledger.
- 79.8 s, 7.74 s: To cut database writes, it saves, called flush in the code, once every five hundred records, and all three campaigns share that batch.
- 87.82 s, 4.63 s: Until then, records wait in a buffer, and spent only reads what has been saved.
- 92.73 s, 2.52 s: So pacing can keep serving until the next save.
- 95.53 s, 3.41 s: The US campaign alone ends at one hundred five percent.
- 99.22 s, 4.33 s: Tokyo alone climbs from one hundred fifty to one hundred seventy-five.
- 103.83 s, 3.2 s: Together, with the shared batch, that is the one hundred eighty-one.

### 05-tests  (107.75 s to 128.47 s, 59 words; while speaking, 276 syllables a minute, 192 words a minute)

- 108.15 s, 1.62 s: So why did every test pass?
- 110.06 s, 6.93 s: The throughput agent rebuilt the older tests to save after every record, so none of them ran pacing against real batching.
- 117.27 s, 3.18 s: None of the agents' tests ran the three campaigns together.
- 120.73 s, 2.03 s: Only a reviewer's contract test does.
- 123.03 s, 4.71 s: Euro and yen fail it, and both failures are marked todo, so the suite stays green.

### 06-fix  (128.47 s to 154.73 s, 78 words; while speaking, 275 syllables a minute, 197 words a minute)

- 128.87 s, 2.22 s: Here is a fix, tried in a scratch copy.
- 131.37 s, 1.45 s: It is two small changes.
- 133.1 s, 3.05 s: Pacing converts the budget to cents before it compares.
- 136.43 s, 5.7 s: And the ledger's spent adds what is still waiting in the buffer, so batching saves writes without hiding spend.
- 142.41 s, 8.26 s: Rerun the same morning, and all three campaigns land at one hundred percent, a few cents over, since a request is checked before its cost is added.
- 150.94 s, 3.07 s: The contract test passes, with its todo marks removed.

### 07-close  (154.73 s to 170.26 s, 43 words; while speaking, 293 syllables a minute, 194 words a minute)

- 155.13 s, 1.24 s: Nobody was careless.
- 156.65 s, 2.6 s: Each agent tested its own task, and it passed.
- 159.53 s, 3.52 s: The failures lived between the changes, where nobody owned the whole.
- 163.33 s, 2.94 s: So apply both changes, and keep the contract test.
- 166.56 s, 2.99 s: And treat every note as a lead, until the code agrees.
